Are you a resident of Clackamas County and need to understand how the county's court system works? In this article, we'll provide you with a detailed overview of the Clackamas County Circuit Court. What is the Clackamas County Circuit Court?

The Clackamas County Circuit Court is a trial court located in Oregon's Clackamas County. It is one of the 27 circuit courts in the state of Oregon and has jurisdiction over all civil and criminal cases that occur within Clackamas County. The court is responsible for interpreting and enforcing the law within its jurisdiction.

Jurisdiction of the Clackamas County Circuit Court

The Clackamas County Circuit Court has jurisdiction over all civil and criminal cases that occur within Clackamas County. Civil cases are disputes between individuals or organizations, such as lawsuits over contract disputes or personal injury claims. Criminal cases involve the violation of state law and include crimes such as theft, assault, and drug offenses. The Clackamas County Circuit Court also handles juvenile cases and domestic relations cases such as divorce, child custody, and child support.

Structure of the Clackamas County Circuit Court

The Clackamas County Circuit Court is divided into several divisions, including the civil division, criminal division, family law division, and juvenile division. Each division is responsible for handling specific types of cases. The court also has a small claims division for cases involving claims of $10,000 or less.

Judges of the Clackamas County Circuit Court

The Clackamas County Circuit Court is presided over by elected judges who serve six-year terms. The number of judges serving on the court varies based on the workload of the court. Each judge is responsible for hearing cases within their assigned division and making decisions based on the evidence presented in court.

Types of Cases Heard in the Clackamas County Circuit Court

The Clackamas County Circuit Court hears a wide variety of cases, including:

  • Civil cases, such as contract disputes and personal injury claims
  • Criminal cases, such as theft, assault, and drug offenses
  • Juvenile cases, such as delinquency and dependency cases
  • Domestic relations cases, such as divorce, child custody, and child support
  • Small claims cases involving claims of $10,000 or less

Filing a Case in the Clackamas County Circuit Court

To file a case in the Clackamas County Circuit Court, you must first determine which division your case falls under. Once you have determined the appropriate division, you can obtain the necessary forms from the court's website or by visiting the court in person. You must then complete the forms and file them with the court along with the appropriate filing fees.

Appearing in the Clackamas County Circuit Court

If you are required to appear in the Clackamas County Circuit Court, it is important to dress appropriately and arrive on time. You should bring all necessary documents and any evidence related to your case. Failure to appear in court can result in a warrant for your arrest, so it's essential to take your court appearances seriously.
